requirements.requirement: Configure /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory where users cannot remove files owned by other users.
requirements.summary: The directory was created as root:root with mode 1777. An unprivileged UID successfully created a file, while deletion of a root-owned file was denied and the file remained present. The same permissions and behavior were directly reconfirmed after reboot.

overall_summary: The task outcome is satisfied with direct permission and behavioral testing. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: node1 was healthy before restart, the restart was acknowledged, its boot ID changed from 6d37896c-e0cd-4fe7-acbf-94fc35781e09 to 9004a381-9ba8-4c80-a1d3-16eab6cac9f4, and system health, directory state, stored data, writability, and deletion protection recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart. The only notable issue is leftover test residue.
limitations: Testing used UID 65534 as the unprivileged user rather than multiple named user accounts; mode 1777 and the direct write/deletion tests nevertheless provide strong evidence of the requested general behavior.
The lifecycle snapshot inventories /tmp but not /srv/drop, so retained proof files are established by the final executor command rather than independently inventoried by the lifecycle collector.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unnecessary system mutation was identified: creating the directory served the task, test files supported bounded behavioral and persistence evidence, and the reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. However, evidence artifacts were not cleaned up: root-owned-proof and user-owned-proof from cmd-7fe22270f328468a, post-reboot-user-proof from cmd-fde5d70ecca54aac, and /tmp/drop-rm-error plus /tmp/post-reboot-rm-error from those commands remained after execution. These are low-risk but unwanted residues. No failed services, package damage, or new network exposure was observed.
